title: Weyl-Titchmarsh M-function as Herglotz master of the Sturm-Liouville Green kernel
expression_sketch: Half-line Weyl-Titchmarsh matrix M_+(z, x0), z in C \ R. Herglotz: Im M_+(z, x0) > 0 for z in C+ (upper half-plane); M_+(conjugate(z), x0) = M_+(z, x0)^*; rank M_+ = m; lim_{eps->0+} M_+(lambda + I*eps, x0) exists for a.e. lambda in R. Isolated poles of M_+ and of -M_+**(-1) are at most first order, real, with nonpositive residue. Scalar Green kernel (separated endpoints): G(z, x, x') = psi_left(z, x_<)*psi_right(z, x_>) / W(psi_left, psi_right) for z in C \ R, with Wronskian W = m_left(z) - m_right(z). Diagonal Green g(z, x) = G(z, x, x) is itself Herglotz in z. Weyl solution: psi(z, x) = theta(z, x) + m(z)*phi(z, x), square-integrable at the singular end for Im z != 0.
latent_structure: A Herglotz-Nevanlinna master M(z) holomorphic off the real axis interpolates the resolvent/Green kernel of a Sturm-Liouville (or Dirac) operator. Boundary values eps -> 0+ recover the spectral measure; poles on R are eigenvalues. Left and right Weyl solutions with Wronskian of two m-functions reconstruct G, so generic x < x' and diagonal x = x' are members of one Green family, not CSE of two fundamental solutions.

z.notes: spectral parameter of M and of the Green kernel

x0.notes: reference point on the half-line / interval

lambda.notes: real energy at which boundary values of M are taken

m.notes: matrix size in the Dirac/matrix-valued Schrödinger setting of Clark-Gesztesy

function_domains.M_plus: half-line Weyl-Titchmarsh matrix, Herglotz of maximal rank
function_domains.G: Green kernel of the self-adjoint realization, z in the resolvent set

nonzero_conditions.statement: Wronskian in the Green formula is m_left(z) - m_right(z); equivalently W(psi_left, psi_right) != 0 off the spectrum
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Gesztesy, CASAT 2022 notes: W(psi_{alpha,b,delta}, psi_{alpha,a,gamma}) = m_{alpha,a,gamma}(z,x0) - m_{alpha,b,delta}(z,x0), z in C \ R

positivity_conditions.statement: Im M_+(z, x0) > 0 for z in the open upper half-plane C+
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8(i): Im(M_+(z, x0)) > 0, z in C+

analytic_domains.statement: M_+(z, x0) is a matrix-valued Herglotz function of maximal rank (in particular holomorphic in C+)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8, display (2.19)

analytic_domains.statement: Isolated poles of M_+ and of -M_+**(-1) are at most of first order, are real, and have a nonpositive residue
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8: 'Isolated poles of M_+(z,x0) and -M_+(z,x0)^{-1} are at most of first order, are real, and have a nonpositive residue'

analytic_domains.statement: Green kernel G(z, x, x') is written for z in C \ R (equivalently z in the resolvent set)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Gesztesy, CASAT 2022 notes: G_{gamma,delta}(z,x,x') displayed for z in C \ R

branch_conventions: C+ = {z : Im z > 0}. Herglotz means holomorphic C+ -> {matrices with positive imaginary part}.
Weyl solution uses the L2 (limit-point) or boundary-condition (limit-circle/regular) selection at the far endpoint.

limit_domains.statement: lim_{eps down 0} M_+(lambda + I*eps, x0) exists for a.e. lambda in R
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8, display (2.21)

source_provenance: Clark, S. and Gesztesy, F., Weyl-Titchmarsh M-function asymptotics for matrix-valued Schrödinger operators, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8
Gesztesy, F., Sturm-Liouville and Schrödinger operators: Weyl-Titchmarsh theory, CASAT 2022 lecture notes (JKU), Green function and m-function identities
Titchmarsh, E. C., Eigenfunction Expansions Associated with Second-Order Differential Equations, Oxford, 1946/1962

derived_conditions.statement: The diagonal Green g(z, x) = G(z, x, x) is a scalar Herglotz function of z for each fixed x
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Gesztesy CASAT 2022 notes: 'For each x, the diagonal Green's function ... is a Nevanlinna-Herglotz function'; follows from Im M > 0 on C+

public_source: Clark and Gesztesy, arXiv:math/9905070, Theorem 2.8 (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905070); Titchmarsh, Eigenfunction Expansions (Oxford); Weyl, Math. Ann. 68 (1910) 220-269.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can share the product of two fundamental solutions. LGG antiunifies left and right Weyl solutions. The scientific object is a Herglotz M-function on C \ R whose Wronskian reconstructs the Green kernel for both x < x' and the diagonal.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant 'Weyl-Titchmarsh', 'Herglotz', or 'm-function' as gold names. Do not package as Cauchy-Dunford (mp-cauchy-dunford-01) or as Helmholtz outgoing Green (ac-r03).
notes: Not Helmholtz outgoing Green. Not Cauchy-Dunford contour of a Banach resolvent. Analytic domain C \ R and Im M > 0 on C+ are written in Clark-Gesztesy Theorem 2.8, not folklore i epsilon. The eps down 0+ boundary value of M is the Herglotz inversion, written as (2.21). is_guo=false.
